lines.say: We score each interaction by its effect on each species: plus, minus or zero.
Competition is minus minus. Predation and parasitism are plus minus.
Mutualism is plus plus. Commensalism is plus zero.
Each one changes survival or reproduction. So each is a selection pressure.
Competitive exclusion: two species can't share exactly the same limiting resources forever.
Fundamental niche is the dream. Realised niche is the reality, with competitors.
Barnacle P lives only high on the rocks while Q is present.

draw.alt: Barnacle P only in upper zone when Q present

lines.say: Remove Q, and P spreads down. 45 percent in the middle, 30 at the bottom.

draw.alt: Q removed, P spreads into middle and lower zones

lines.say: Species can share by resource partitioning. Over time this drives character displacement.
Galápagos finches have more different beaks where they live together.
Predators select for prey defences. Prey defences select for better predators.
Camouflage, like the tawny frogmouth, or bright warning colours.
Batesian is a bluffer: a harmless hoverfly looks like a wasp.
Müllerian is a mutual warning: harmful species all look alike.
Plants use spines and secondary compounds, like eucalyptus oils. Koalas tolerate them.
Where cane toads have been longer, snakes show changes against big gapes.
Mutualism helps both. Think Rhizobium in legume roots, or corals with algae.
But each partner wants maximum gain for minimum cost. Cheaters steal nectar.
Legumes cut oxygen to nodules that fix little nitrogen. That punishes cheats.
Parasites live on or in a host. Ticks are ectoparasites, tapeworms endoparasites.
Parasites breed fast, so they can evolve quickly.
Coevolution is reciprocal change. Each species selects the other.
Newt toxin and snake resistance rise together. Region 3 is a hotspot.

draw.alt: Paired bars of toxin and resistance across four regions

lines.say: But correlation isn't proof. Show both traits are heritable and affect survival.
Red Queen: keep evolving just to stay in the same place.
Figs and fig wasps are a coevolved mutualism.
Evolution isn't perfect. It's limited by variation, history, trade-offs and environment.
Bright colours attract mates, but also predators. That's a trade-off.
Nothing evolves in order to survive. Selection acts on existing variation.
One species adapting to another isn't coevolution. Both must change.
